items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: You see, myself, we played at the ringside with Sharky. And we had one, I'll tell you how good that band was.

ctx.x: Fifty years ago did they have a lot of solos? They start out an ensemble and everybody plays the same.

For, listen, for is drum solos. I'm going to put it on a drum. That only came a few years back as drum solos. Then a drum player never did play a drum solo in my years. All he done was play drums and give that band the tempo. When that band hit one, two, that leader hit one, two, three, four, there he was. If it wasn't with the sticks, it was the brushes, but mostly the brushes. You understand? items.title: Sharkey Bonano Interview, 1966-11-09
items.q: So we all made the records. Sidney Airdin, Joe Larcanna, I think it was Monk Hazel, Chink Martin.

ctx.x: He had the records. Very good. And he got the session. So we all made the records. Sidney Airdin, Joe Larcanna, I think it was Monk Hazel, Chink Martin.
